abstract:
Polycrisis Resilience – Global Warming in the Global South is a foundational publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).
It examines the climate–population–development feedback system across seven Global South regions and three multi-century analytical horizons (21st century, 22nd century, and 23rd century and beyond), positioning Polycrisis Resilience as a development-oriented response to compounding climate and demographic pressures.

keyFindings.title: Polycrisis Resilience must account for the long-term convergence of climate change, population growth, and development disparities across the Global South; temperature rise alone does not determine harm—development, infrastructure, and institutional capacity do.

Under UN World Population Prospects 2024, Sub-Saharan Africa is projected to grow from 1.22 billion in 2024 to 2.20 billion in 2054 and 3.34 billion by 2100, making front-loaded clean energy, resilient cities, water, and health infrastructure decisive for future vulnerability.

Physical climate commitments—especially multi-century sea-level rise from deep-ocean warming and ice-sheet melt—persist across the 21st, 22nd, and 23rd+ centuries even after global temperatures stabilize, requiring multi-generational coastal and agricultural adaptation.

Deploying six development-oriented interventions (climate adaptation, technology diffusion, sustainable convergence, human development, infrastructure, and institutional resilience) cuts composite Global South vulnerability from 68.0 (2025) to 20.0 by 2100 and 12.0 by 2300 (-82.4%).
